title: WBW Latin America Organizer Addresses UN Human Rights Council Event in Geneva
content:
Demilitarization, Europe, Latin America, What to do, Why End War, World

By Gabriel Aguirre, World BEYOND War, October 1, 2026

First, I would like to express my gratitude to the organizers of this side event, held within the framework of the 63rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council. We find ourselves at a critical juncture where international law is being openly disregarded by various States, through conduct that places international stability and order at grave risk.

I firmly join the voices of the colleagues who spoke before me regarding the urgent need to defend human rights in every corner of the globe, without selectivity or double standards. We are witnessing a progressive weakening of the United Nations with every action that violates the most fundamental norms of global coexistence.

War, the arms race, and militarism are prevailing over diplomacy, negotiation, and peaceful coexistence. For our organization, it is alarming that the world currently allocates 2.87 trillion dollars to military spending, representing 2.5% of global GDP. In the last year alone, military spending in Europe grew by 14%, while the United States remains the country with the largest global military budget, reaching 954 billion dollars.

These figures confront us with the painful reality of a world preparing for armed conflict, while the primary victims remain the most vulnerable

On World Teachers’ Day, we want to begin with a simple message: 

Thank you.




To teachers, facilitators, trainers, youth workers, community educators and everyone helping people learn, question and act: thank you for the work you do.




This year’s 

World Teachers’ Day theme

What kind of future are we educating for?




Education shapes how we understand peace, conflict, security and war; what futures we can imagine; and what we believe we can change.




At 

World BEYOND War

, education is one of the main ways we work for change.




We call our approach 

pro-peace and anti-war education

: helping people develop the knowledge, skills, relationships and collective capacity to build peace and contribute to more peaceful, just and inclusive societies, while critically examining the systems, institutions, cultural norms and interests that prepare for, normalize and sustain war.




The aim is not to tell people what to think, but to help them question, imagine alternatives and build the confidence and capacity to act — individually and together.

title: 10 Reasons to Oppose the “Arc de Trump”
content:
Culture of Peace, North America

By Medea Benjamin, September 30, 2026

There was already widespread opposition to Trump’s proposed arch at Memorial Circle in Arlington, Virginia—a 250-foot structure, roughly the height of a 20-story building and 50 percent taller than Paris’s Arc de Triomphe. Now the controversy has intensified: Trump says the arch, which originally included plans for an observation deck, a café, a gift shop and exhibition space, would also function as a military complex, housing drones, snipers and ammunition.

Here are 10 reasons (really 9 plus your own) to oppose the “Arc de Trump.”

1. It would overwhelm one of America’s most important historic landscapes. The giant arch would sit directly on the ceremonial axis connecting Arlington House, Arlington National Cemetery, Memorial Bridge and the Lincoln Memorial, dramatically altering this historic view and dwarfing the surrounding monuments rather than complementing them.

2. It clashes with the very meaning of the site. Arlington Memorial Bridge and the surrounding landscape were conceived as symbols of national reconciliation after the Civil War. And Arlington National Cemetery is a solemn resting place for hundreds of thousands of service members. author: David Swanson
title: Trump’s Offer to Sell Weapons to China Is Wonderful
content:
Asia, Demilitarization, North America, Stop Arms Trade, World

By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, September 30, 2026

Wednesday morning I was speaking by Zoom to a college class about war and peace, and one of the students asked about the risk of the U.S. demilitarizing and other nations not. I gave a standard answer about how a reverse arms race could be done in stages. The U.S. could commit to not spending more than three times any other nation on its military and proceed downward from there. Of the couple of dozen nations that spend much of anything on their militaries, all but three are U.S. allies and weapons customers being hammered hard by the U.S. government (and NATO) to spend more. The only country spending more than a tiny fraction of the U.S. — in fact, spending close to a third of U.S. military spending as it’s usually reported or a sixth of what it really is — is China. If the U.S. were to keep its nukes out of South Korea and Japan, and its troops out of South Korea, and finally end the war and turn South Korea’s military over to South Korea, and start joining treaties and courts and beginning a general disarmament, North Korea would almost certainly join in serious negotiations about getting rid of its nukes, while China would — I guaranteed to this college class — not keep increasing its own military spending.

author: David Swanson
title: One Down! Abolishing Dueling and Warmaking
content:
By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, September 29, 2026




According to an 1838 U.S.-published instruction manual for dueling, the practice of dueling was going to last “as long as a manly independence, and a lofty personal pride in all that dignifies and ennobles the human character, shall continue to exist.”[1] Be that as it may, dueling was soon gone as a practice in any way acceptable or routine, and most of the globe had never had it to begin with.




Many years ago, I wrote a book about the outlawrists of the 1920s, people (led by lawyers) who were fond of pointing out that dueling had been outlawed and abolished, and so could war be. Yet dueling had persisted for centuries in Europe and in the United States despite laws forbidding it as murder. And we’ve now gone a century with laws forbidding war, while the wars persist.




I do not doubt for a minute that laws helped end dueling. Nobody could have finally begun using the laws had there not been any. Nobody could have denounced dueling as a crime had it not been a crime. But I’ve encountered over the years numerous cursory accounts of dueling that explain its demise in very simple terms, albeit each explanation different from all the others. title: Podcast: Beyond Borders with Khawaja Hammad Akbar (#NoWar2026 Preview)
content:
Asia, Culture of Peace, Demilitarization, How I Became a Peace Activist, Myth of Necessity, Nonviolent Activism, Podcasts, World BEYOND War Podcast

By Marc Eliot Stein, September 26, 2026, World BEYOND War

“Beyond Borders” is the theme of World BEYOND War’s #NoWar2026 online conference next month. To preview this conference, I spoke with Khawaja Hammad Akbar, a peace builder in Pakistan who will be leading a panel on case studies of militarized borders and demilitarized zones with speakers from Korea, Gaza and the US/Mexico border.

What does it mean to seek a world “beyond borders”? To begin exploring this question, I asked Khawaja about his own background and motivations for antiwar work and discovered that his interest began (as it so often does) with his desire to understand his own family legacy. As we talked about the devastation and trauma left behind by the 1947 India/Pakistan partition, a familiar pattern became clear: the borders of the past still imprison all of us.

We also talked about popular attitudes about militarism in our own societies, about our hopes for a better future, and about the inspiration of past teachers of peace like Syed Ahmad Khan. The closing music is an excerpt from a live recording of “Ballot Box” by Penboy, a singer and spoken word poet who will be performing at the #NoWar2026 conference which takes place October 23, 24 and 25.

By Medea Benjamin and Nicolas J. S. Davies, World BEYOND War, September 22, 2026

The Trump administration came perilously close to launching another bombing campaign against Yemen this weekend. According to a September 20 New York Times report, US commanders had approved their targets, American troops were loading bombs onto warplanes, and an attack on Yemen’s Ansar Allah forces was about to begin when President Trump abruptly reversed course.

For two weeks, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had been pleading with Trump to intervene as Ansar Allah (Houthi) forces swept through Saudi-backed forces’ positions along Yemen’s Red Sea coast. Trump initially resisted, but after another urgent call from the Saudi crown prince, he instructed the Pentagon to prepare for airstrikes. By Sunday, he had changed his mind again, at least temporarily.

The New York Times reported that many of Trump’s closest advisers opposed joining the Saudi war. U.S. military officials also questioned whether renewed bombing would accomplish anything, given that Ansar Allah had withstood more than 1,000 U.S. strikes during a seven-week campaign in 2025. That operation consumed roughly $1 billion in munitions and other military resources in its first month alone.

Together with Kilusan para sa Pambansang Demokrasya, World BEYOND War commemorated the 45th International Day of Peace in Manilla with a public event held at a wall of remembrance bearing the names of many anti-martial-law heroes in the Philippines.

In the Philippines, the day also marked the 54th Commemoration of the Declaration of Martial Law. For 14 years, the country and its people suffered from militaristic rule, from which they still carry the effects in the form of corruption, political patronage, and elitism.

title: Don’t Look Away
content:
Displaced Palestinians staying in flimsy tents. Photo by Zyad Abu Mariam, courtesy of Norwegian Refugee Council.

By Kathy Kelly, World BEYOND War, September 15, 2026

Over the past two years, World BEYOND War members have been grateful to ally with a coalition called Global Solidarity for Peace in Palestine. In weekly online meetings, Palestinians living in the West Bank update our coordinating committee about their experiences amidst ongoing, U.S. provisioned Israeli genocide against Palestinians. They speak with anguish about people in the West Bank and Gaza enduring siege, hunger, disease, forcible displacement, bereavement, poisoning, contamination, and the frustrations of an Occupying force that constantly wages pogrom-style attacks.

Our Palestinian coalition members living in the West Bank long to extend a helping hand to people trapped in Gaza. They recently raised the dilemma of Gazan children who have already lost years of education. Many live in wretched tent encampments, lack adequate food and medicine, and struggle with psycho-social traumas because of having lost their loved ones.

title: On October 20th, Tell the U.S. Government to End the War on Iran
content:

By Action Corps, Bring Our Troops Home, Common Defense, The Libertarian Institute, MPower Change Action Fund, National Iranian American Council (NIAC), Peace Action, Presbyterian Church (USA) Office of Public Witness, RootsAction, and World BEYOND War, September 13, 2026

We call on organizations and individuals across the U.S. to gather at their nearest congressional office two weeks before the election, on Tuesday, October 20th, 30 minutes before the office opens for the day, and ask their members of Congress to take action to stop the war against Iran, as described at the bottom of this form.

WHY: If a peace deal with Iran isn’t reached ahead of the U.S. midterm election, we are at risk of the war against Iran becoming a forever war. We need decisive action by our members of Congress to stop the war.

author: David Swanson
title: The Cost of Arms Deals and Corruption in Cameroon
content:
Africa, Cameroon Chapter, Chapters, Economic Cost, Stop Arms Trade

By Guy Feugap, Africa Organizer for World BEYOND War, Corruption Tracker, September 13, 2026

When corruption scandals erupt in the arms trade, attention focuses on the millions embezzled, the officials implicated, and the ensuing legal proceedings. Yet the true cost of these cases often runs much deeper. Behind opaque contracts and illicit commissions lie consequences that directly affect governance, citizens’ trust in their institutions, and, above all, the security of the population. The Defex case, which brought to light corrupt practices in arms contracts between Spain and Cameroon, offers an opportunity to question a security model based on the accumulation of weapons. The Cameroonian case shows that corruption in the arms trade undermines public finances and jeopardizes human security; it thus raises a fundamental question: Can lasting peace truly be built on the foundations of militarism?

In the arms deals between Spain and Cameroon, a financial scandal has implicated high-ranking officials in the Cameroonian government, as documented by Corruption Tracker, which released the report Defex’s Dirty Decades: Arms Sales to Cameroon in September 2025. By World BEYOND War, September 11, 2026

This week, the University of Wisconsin – Madison student chapter of World BEYOND War tabled at the campus student organization fair. They met other students who are also energized to help build a mass antiwar movement. They shared this pie chart of Trump’s proposed budget for 2027, and invited students to show their own priorities for the federal budget by allocating beans between jars. Funding war was not popular!

The students publicized their upcoming Walk for Peace on September 20 in Madison, in solidarity with people around the world marking the International Day of Peace.
